newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico union hails limited petrochemical sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Mexico union hails limited petrochemical sell-off.

text.p: Mexico's powerful oil workers union claimed victory Monday after the government decided to offer minority stakes in 61 petrochemical plants rather than privatising them, as previously planned.
"In principle we believe we got everything we asked for," oil union spokesman Victor Manuel Garcia told Reuters.
President Ernesto Zedillo's government had insisted it would sell off all of the so-called secondary petrochemical operations of Pemex, the state-owned oil company.

But in the face of fierce political opposition, it retreated Sunday, saying it would offer stakes of up to 49 percent in existing plants, though it would allow new facilities to be 100 percent owned by private capital.

Garcia said the oil union's president, Senator Carlos Antonio Romero Deschamps, had made a speech earlier in the day at the political council of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) announcing the union's support for the government's revised strategy.
"It's really good that (the government) complied with what (we) had requested," Garcia said.
Asked if the union would now unconditionally support the government's revised plans for petrochemicals, Garcia said that was likely.
A final decision would depend on the actual texts of the government's legislative proposals, which had yet to be released, he added.
